title: Platform Engineering vs. SRE
subtitle: Explicit platform-SRE contracts and SLOs stop seam debt and make tension productive.

panels.heading: Where the Boundary Fails
panels.caption: Blurred missions create seam debt: upgrades collide, gates stall, and no one owns incidents.
panels.note: Write the boundary or you inherit outages from assumptions and invisible queues.

panels.heading: Missions and Time Horizons
panels.caption: Platform serves devs with paved paths; SRE owns user SLOs, error budgets, and incidents.
panels.note: Treat the platform like any dependency, with SLIs, budgets, and clear escalations.

panels.heading: Contracts Make Tension Useful
panels.caption: Publish SLIs/SLOs, tie budgets to change policy, and predefine rollback and deprecation.
panels.note: Good fences are paved paths plus testable contracts and shared KPIs.

strip_title: How to make the boundary real and durable
strip_caption: Turn blurred goodwill into productized contracts, shared SLIs, and budgeted change.
